original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Prove or falsify a no-paid-rank-saving theorem for any number of binary scalar registers, rational rank-one address frames with at most one independent rational relation, and a diagonal monomial endpoint; emphasize four registers and four-dimensional targets.
scope_change_reason: Enlarge the predecessor three-register model to four and arbitrary register counts, while restricting frame-relation nullity to zero or one. This is a scoped obstruction, not a general four-register lower bound.
bottleneck_link: A four-register rank-four mechanism would need fewer than 16 rank-one paid calls. A uniform obstruction in the one-relation class rules out a concrete search family even with scalar mixing and restored dirty registers free in the optimistic model.
stop_rule: One uniform proof attempt with exact symbolic controls; do not enumerate arbitrary rational frames or reopen the completed three-register search. Stop research after 33 minutes and reserve at least the last 12 minutes of the 45-minute budget for verification and handoff.
evidence: README.md proves the arbitrary-register theorem. CERTIFICATE.json contains the complete 1..4-register projector census, 577 exact conjugation checks, thirteen rational formal-word fixtures and nine hypothesis/scope controls, replayed by separate implementations.
author: Hanson Sun (@bbMisk), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human review is claimed.
